newsitem.title: USA: NYS Gov wants full share of federal highway funds.
newsitem.headline: NYS Gov wants full share of federal highway funds.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki Thursday pushed ahead with an effort to ensure the state gets all its federal highway and transit funds, naming his transportation commissioner to lead the campaign.

The state stands to lose from $300 million to as much as $1.5 billion unless the present draft of the federal Intermodal Surface Transportation Highway Efficiency (ISTEA) of 1991, which expires on September 30, is amended.
"Protecting New York's ISTEA funding is one of my highest priorities because of its potential impact on the state's infrastructure and continued economic expansion," Pataki said in prepared remarks.
John Daly, who has served as the transportation commissioner since January 1995, will leave his post, effective immediately, to protect New York State's interests during the debate in Congress.
A spokesman for the state transportation department said that First Deputy Commissioner, Joseph Boardman, will take over as the agency's acting head.

The transportation spokesman said that Daly is expected to push for an approximately $1 billion proposal to link the Long Island Railroad with New York City's Grand Central terminal, a plan that has the backing of U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato, a Republican.
"That will be one of the things the commissioner will help coordinate, the various projects around the state," the spokesman explained.
Controversies over how New York State splits federal funds with New York City likely will be another issue.

The state transportation department presently gets about $1.1 billion of federal funds for highways, while the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, which runs mass transit for the city and downstate, gets approximately $700 million.
New York State was part of a 15-state coalition of Northeast states that will lobby for federal funds as a group.
